messages:
Jessie: Heads up — seeing ~6 GPU nodes in eu-west1 go NotReady. kubelet logs show nvidia-driver-init timeout and nvidia-device-plugin failing to register. infra-bot reports a huge CSR backlog (~260 pending). Cluster-autoscaler says pool gpuprod-eu-west1 is unschedulable. Anyone seen this pattern?
Matt: Can you paste `kubectl get nodes` and `kubectl get csr | grep Pending | wc -l`?
Jessie: Sure, output: 
```
# kubectl get nodes
gpu-eu-1a-3   NotReady   3d   v1.27.4   <...>
gpu-eu-1a-4   NotReady   3d
gpu-eu-1b-1   NotReady   2d
# kubectl get csr | grep Pending | wc -l
260
```
Li: 260 pending CSRs is the giveaway. We had apiserver CPU spikes earlier which delays CSR approval controller. Could be cert-rotator/controller-manager churn creating duplicate CSRs during driver restarts.
Sara: FYI autoscaler flagged the pool as blocked: all nodes tainted NoSchedule by device-plugin init and pods are Pending. If we leave this long preemptible churn will bump cost and reduce capacity.
Matt: Quick unblock steps: try approving a single CSR for one node and restart the device-plugin daemonset on that node's kubelet to let it register. If that works, we can batch-approve.
Jessie: Doing that now —
```
kubectl get csr | grep gpu-eu-1a-3
kubectl certificate approve csr-abc123
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart ds/nvidia-device-plugin
```
Jessie: After approving & restart one node is back Ready. infra-bot: node/gpu-eu-1a-3 -> Ready :white_check_mark:
infra-bot: node/gpu-eu-1a-3 pod/nvidia-device-plugin -> Running
Li: Good. Root cause hypothesis: during the driver rollout the nodes attempted to renew certificates but the approver loop got overloaded and CSRs queued. device-plugin waits for certs and fails init, taints node. That cascades into autoscaler thinking pool can't accept new workloads.
Matt: Immediate mitigation plan I recommend: 1) Approve CSRs for impacted nodes (batched, 10-20 at a time). 2) Restart nvidia-device-plugin DaemonSet after approve to force registration. 3) Temporarily relax autoscaler safeguards (or set scale-up delay) to avoid flapping. 4) Roll back the driver rollout config to serial strategy (maxUnavailable=1) for gpuprod pools.
Sara: I'm opening infra ticket and a PR for the rollout change + an alert on CSR queue > 50. https://go.redwood/infra/issue/9242 :eyes:
Li: Longer term: add backpressure to cert-rotator + controller rate limits, and a guard in the approver that rejects obviously-duplicated CSRs or rate-limits from same node id. Also add an exporter metric for csr_queue_length.
Jessie: Approved 6 CSRs and restarted ds across the affected nodes — all recovered, autoscaler cleared the blockage. Leaving monitoring on for 1hr. Thanks all.
Matt: Nice work. Please paste logs into the incident doc and include the CSR IDs for postmortem.
Jessie: Will do, adding to /docs/incidents/gpu-csr-backlog-2030456789.md
oncall-bot: Reminder — oncall rotation: Matt oncall until 22:00 UTC
Sara: Adding playbook steps for future rollouts to avoid >5% pool churn at once. :thumbsup:
Jessie: Closing thread for now, will reopen if it recurs.
